text: Every morning I lay on the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> In the front parlour. <break time="0.8s" /> Watching her door. <break time="0.8s" /> Keeping the blind pulled down. <break time="0.8s" /> To within an inch of the sash. <break time="0.8s" /> So that I could not be seen. <break time="0.8s" /> When she came out on the doorstep. <break time="0.8s" /> My heart leaped. <break time="0.8s" /> And I ran to the hall. <break time="0.8s" /> Seized my books. <break time="0.8s" /> And followed her. <break time="0.8s" /> Always keeping her brown figure in my eye. <break time="0.8s" /> I had never spoken to her. <break time="0.8s" /> Except for a few casual words. <break time="0.8s" /> And yet her name. <break time="0.8s" /> Was like a summons. <break time="0.8s" /> To all my foolish blood. <break time="0.8s" /> Her image accompanied me. <break time="0.8s" /> Even in places. <break time="0.8s" /> The most hostile to romance. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as the crowded market. <break time="0.8s" /> Where my aunt went shopping. <break time="0.8s" /> On Saturday evenings. <break time="0.8s" /> We walked through the flaring streets. <break time="0.8s" /> Jostled by drunken men. <break time="0.8s" /> And bargaining women. <break time="0.8s" /> Amid the curses of labourers. <break time="0.8s" /> And the shrill cries of shop boys. <break time="0.8s" /> These noises converged. <break time="0.8s" /> In a single sensation of life. <break time="0.8s" /> For me and I imagined. <break time="0.8s" /> That I bore my chalice safely. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a throng of foes. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening I went. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the back drawing room. <break time="0.8s" /> In which the priest had died. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was a dark, rainy evening. <break time="0.8s" /> And there was no sound in the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Pressing the palms of my hands together. <break time="0.8s" /> Until they trembled. <break time="0.8s" /> I murmured. <break time="0.8s" /> O love, O love, many times.
